Supervised Feature Screening via Marginal Cox Model

Source: R/variable_screening.R
supervised_screening.Rd

Implements marginal screening for high-dimensional omics features based on their association with survival outcomes. Features are selected by one of four criteria or a fixed top-N.

Usage

supervised_screening(
  data,
  clinical_data,
  rank = c("pval", "absmg", "padj", "mgpval"),
  p_threshold = 0.05,
  top_n_features = NULL
)

Arguments

data

Numeric matrix of omics data (features as rows, samples as columns). Row names must be set.

clinical_data

Matrix or data frame of clinical data (variables as rows, samples as columns). Must contain rows "overall_survival" and "status".

rank

Character string specifying the ranking criterion:

  • "pval": p-value of the marginal Cox test. Supports p_threshold and top_n_features.

  • "padj": Benjamini-Hochberg adjusted p-value. Supports p_threshold and top_n_features.

  • "absmg": absolute marginal Cox coefficient \(|\hat\beta_j|\). Requires top_n_features.

  • "mgpval": combined score \(-\log_{10}(p) \times |\hat\beta_j|\). Requires top_n_features.

Default is "pval".

p_threshold

Numeric threshold used only when rank is "pval" (p-value \(\le\) threshold) or "padj" (BH-adjusted p-value \(\le\) threshold), and top_n_features is NULL. Default is 0.05.

top_n_features

Integer. Number of top-ranked features to retain. Mandatory for "absmg" and "mgpval", which have no natural threshold. Optional for "pval" and "padj" (overrides p_threshold when set). Default is NULL.

Value

A named list with:

  • data: Filtered matrix (selected features x samples), with original (non-standardised) values.

  • rank_table: Data frame with columns feature, beta, p_value, p_adj, score (\(-\log_{10}(p) \times |\beta|\)), rank_value (the metric used for sorting), and rank_position, for all features.

  • selected: Character vector of selected feature names.

  • rank: The rank argument used.

Details

Designed to be reused across omics prepare_* functions (mRNA, miRNA, CNV, Methylation).
